title: Proof of Estimate: an on-chain crowd forecast
summary: Create a yes/no poll, give your estimate as a range, and watch the program fold it into a weighted crowd estimate stored on-chain.
what: Proof of Estimate (POE) is a forecasting app. Anyone creates a yes/no question. Forecasters answer with a **range** (for example 30–70% likely). The program turns each range into a point estimate (the midpoint) and an uncertainty (the width), stakes 100 POEKEN from the forecaster, and updates the poll's **collective estimate**, a weighted running average, inside the same transaction. Every new user gets 1,000 POEKEN from a mint the program itself controls.
app_note: The fork's own Next.js 14 app (`app/`), static export. Changes: base path, the IDL generated from the program at this commit (the committed app IDL was from a later version), and `/poll/?id=` instead of `/poll/[id]` so it works on static hosting.

try_steps.do: Open [the app](/dapps/poe-solana/) and connect Phantom with the button in the top bar.
try_steps.see: The POE home page with the poll list; the sidebar has Home, My Polls, Create Polls, and a **Mint Poeken** button while your wallet is not registered.

try_steps.do: Click **Create Polls**. Type a Question and a Description, pick a Category and a Duration, press **Submit** and approve.
try_steps.see: One transaction holding **two** instructions, `register_user` then `create_poll` (the app adds `register_user` because you are new). The toast says "Poll created." You now hold 1,000 POEKEN.
ran: Create Poll + Submit sent `register_user` + `create_poll` in one tx

try_steps.do: Go back to **Home** and find your poll card. Drag the estimate slider to set a range, then press **Submit Estimate** and approve.
try_steps.see: A `make_estimate` transaction. 100 POEKEN leave your wallet for the program's escrow, and the card shows the crowd estimate and "1 forecaster" read back from the poll account.
ran: Submit Estimate sent `make_estimate`; the card then read back Yes 60%, 1 forecaster, 1 estimate

try_steps.do: Switch Phantom to a second account, open the same poll and submit a different range.
try_steps.see: The second transaction again starts with `register_user` (new wallet). The crowd estimate moves toward your number, but by less than a plain average if your range is wide: wide ranges carry less weight.
try_steps.ran_note: Not clicked through yet with a second wallet.

try_steps.do: Open the poll's detail page (the card links to `/poll/?id=<n>`).
try_steps.see: The poll with its estimate history, one entry per `make_estimate`.
try_steps.ran_note: Checked read-only: `/poll/?id=0` showed the poll and its estimate history.

instructions.name: `register_user`: account + 1,000 POEKEN
steps: `init` at `["user", payer]`: one user account per wallet. A second `register_user` from the same wallet fails because the address is already in use (custom program error 0x0, see Proof).
`init_if_needed` creates the wallet's associated token account for POEKEN.

`mint_to` is called with `new_with_signer` and the seeds `["poeken_mint", bump]`: the mint's authority is the mint PDA itself, so only this program can mint, and it mints 1000 × 10⁹ base units = 1,000 POEKEN.

instructions.name: `create_poll`: a poll at a counter-derived address
steps: The poll's seeds are `["poll", state.num_polls.to_le_bytes()]`: poll 0, poll 1, poll 2… each get a predictable address that any client can compute without an index.
`space = Poll::len(&question, &description)` sizes the account to the exact text you typed.
It records the creator, the resolver, the start slot and the decay rate you chose under Duration, then increments `num_polls`, so the next poll gets the next address.

instructions.name: `make_estimate`: stake, record, and update the crowd number
steps: Midpoint and uncertainty: `estimate = (lower + upper) / 2`, `uncertainty = (upper - lower) / 100`. A 30–70 range gives estimate 50 and uncertainty 0.4.

`init_estimate_account` checks both bounds are ≤ 100 and lower ≤ upper, refuses if the poll has ended, then transfers `betting_amount` (100 POEKEN) from you to the escrow with a token CPI that you authorise as signer.
It computes your `recency_weight` from how many slots have passed since the poll started, saves your bounds and weights in `user_estimate`, and bumps your participation count.
Then `update_collective_estimate` (next section) folds your number into the poll.

Order matters: the subtraction `upper - lower` on line 44 runs **before** the `lower <= upper` assert. With lower 70 and upper 30 the `u16` subtraction underflows, and because the workspace enables `overflow-checks` the program aborts: "Program failed to complete" in the Proof section.

innovation.title: an O(1) weighted crowd estimate, updated on-chain
innovation.text: The program never loops over past estimates. It keeps running totals in the poll account (`accumulated_weights`, `accumulated_weights_squared`, the mean and the variance) and updates them with one formula per estimate, so the cost of an estimate is the same for the first forecaster and the thousandth. Each forecast's weight is `(1 - uncertainty) × your score × recency weight`: confident, reputable and later forecasts count more.
more: The mean update is `new = old + weight × (x - old) / total_weight`, the standard incremental weighted mean. The first forecaster simply sets it (lines 224–241).
Estimates are stored as integers with 4 decimal places (`ESTIMATE_PRECISION = 4`): our 30–70 test estimate was read back as `collective_estimate = 500000`, i.e. 50.0000%.

`recency_weight = exp(decay × slots_since_start / 100000)`, capped at 1,000,000. The Duration you pick when creating a poll is the decay rate (from 11.111 for Minutes down to 0.0029173 for Years, in `app/src/types/options.ts`).
Geometric means for scoring use a lookup table of natural logs, `LOGS[0..=100]` in `constants.rs`, instead of computing `ln` on-chain.

frontend.title: Create Poll: derive every PDA in the browser, prepend `register_user` if needed
steps: The app fetches `poe_state`, reads `numPolls`, and derives the new poll's address with the same seeds as the program: `["poll", numPolls as 8 little-endian bytes]`.
If your `user` account does not exist yet (`getAccountInfo` returns null), it builds a `registerUser` instruction too and sends both in **one** transaction.

frontend.title: Submit Estimate: the same pattern for `make_estimate`
steps: All ten accounts (user, poll, user_estimate, poll_estimate_update, scoring_list, user_score, your token account, mint, escrow) are derived client-side and passed with `accountsPartial`.

frontend.title: Sending: a v0 versioned transaction through the wallet
steps: The instructions are compiled into a `TransactionMessage` v0, wrapped in a `VersionedTransaction` and handed to `wallet.sendTransaction`, so Phantom signs and sends. It sends with `skipPreflight: true`, so a failing transaction is only reported after confirmation.

exercises.title: Compute a poll address
steps: In Node with `@solana/web3.js` and `bn.js`, derive `PublicKey.findProgramAddressSync([Buffer.from('poll'), new BN(0).toArrayLike(Buffer,'le',8)], new PublicKey('6E4atN4EvrvxNtpBQwPMg7AkzJ2TjZrbxBkou9BN99p5'))`.
exercises.expect: `9V1u4vvP4T6JZgEXdag5j49iJRViPSi8PqQfgCisLKhT`, the poll #0 our test created (recorded in the devnet log).
exercises.hint: The poll id is a `u64` stored as 8 little-endian bytes. `new BN(0).toArrayLike(Buffer, 'le', 8)` is eight zero bytes, not the ASCII character `0`.
exercises.approach: `findProgramAddressSync([Buffer.from('poll'), <8-byte id>], programId)`. For id 0 the result must be the recorded poll `9V1u4vvP…`. A different encoding (big-endian, or a 4-byte int) will produce a different address.

exercises.title: Predict the first collective estimate
steps: Create a new poll and submit a range of 20–40 as the first forecaster.
Open the poll account on Explorer, or read it in the app.
exercises.expect: Estimate 30, stored as `collective_estimate = 300000`, with 1 forecaster and 1 estimate update.
exercises.hint: The first forecaster's midpoint becomes the collective estimate with no one to average against. Midpoint is `(lower + upper) / 2`; the on-chain field is stored × 10,000.
exercises.approach: Submit 20–40 on a fresh poll and read `collective_estimate`. It should be 300000 (30.0000). If you submit a second estimate, the value will move, so do this as the first forecaster.

exercises.title: Watch the stake move
steps: Before submitting an estimate, note your POEKEN balance in Phantom.
Submit an estimate on any poll.
exercises.expect: Exactly 100 POEKEN less (the poll's `betting_amount`), now in the program's escrow token account.
exercises.hint: The stake is a token transfer, not a SOL transfer. Watch the POEKEN mint, not your SOL balance.
exercises.approach: Note the POEKEN balance, submit any estimate, and compare: it falls by `betting_amount` (100 in our deploy). The escrow token account, a PDA, rises by the same amount — you can see both sides in the transaction's token balances.

exercises.title: Reproduce the underflow and fix it
steps: In `programs/poe/src/lib.rs`, add `require!(lower_estimate <= upper_estimate, ...)` (with a new error code) as the first line of `make_estimate`, before the subtraction.
`anchor build` and call `make_estimate(70, 30)` from a test.
exercises.expect: Before the fix: "Program failed to complete" (the u16 underflow). After: your named error, raised before any arithmetic.
exercises.hint: The crash is a wrapping `u16` subtraction when `lower > upper`. Guard before the arithmetic, not after.
exercises.approach: Add `require!(lower_estimate <= upper_estimate, PoEError::YourNewError)` at the top of `make_estimate`, rebuild, and call `make_estimate(70, 30)` from a local test. Before the fix the program aborts with a generic overflow; after, you get your named error and no state changes.

exercises.title: See the weight of a wide range
steps: Create two new polls, A and B. With wallet 1, submit 50–50 (one point on the slider) on both.
With wallet 2, submit 90–90 on poll A and 80–100 on poll B (both midpoints are 90).
Compare the two collective estimates.
exercises.expect: Poll A moves further toward 90 than poll B, because weight = (1 − uncertainty) × score × recency and the uncertainty is 0 for 90–90 but 0.2 for 80–100 (recency differs only slightly).
exercises.hint: Weight falls as the range gets wider: uncertainty is `(upper − lower) / 100` on a 0–100 slider, and the weight multiplies by `(1 − uncertainty)`.
exercises.approach: On two fresh polls, have wallet 1 submit 50–50 on both, then wallet 2 submit 90–90 on A and 80–100 on B. A's collective estimate should move further toward 90 than B's, matching the formula in the program. Recency is almost the same if you submit them back to back.

not_covered: Both core actions were clicked through in the hosted app (create poll with registration, submit estimate). Not exercised yet: a second forecaster through the UI, `update_estimate`, `remove_estimate`, and resolving a poll / collecting points (these need the poll's resolver).
objectives: Follow a program-owned mint whose authority is a PDA, and a user account that is created on the first instruction.
See a stake move from a user's token account into an escrow, as a CPI to the Token Program.
Recompute a weighted running average, and fix an underflow when a range is reversed.
prereqs: Phantom on devnet and about 0.1 devnet SOL.
[PulseFund](/lessons/pulsefund-sol/) (PDAs, rent) or equivalent. Some comfort reading Rust `u16`/`u64` arithmetic helps for the underflow exercise.
